JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 10122020 at about 1000 to 10 05 p.m. when deceased was traveling from Bengaluru to Thippanahalli on motor cycle bearing No.KA04JJ9559, driver of the lorry bearing No.HR38Y3353 came with high speed, violently and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, as a result of which Jagadeesha T.R. died on the spot.
Due to death of Jagadeesha, petitioners are struggling and finding it difficult to lead a normal life.
It is further stated that Jagadeesha T.R. was working in Shahi Exports Pvt., Ltd., and petitioners are depending upon the income of deceased.
Hence, petitioners prays to award compensation of Rs.50,96,165/ from the respondents.
3. Inspite of due service of notice of the petition upon them, the respondents No.1 & 2 appeared before this Tribunal.

The respondent No.1 filed written statement wherein contended that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing reg.No.HR 38Y 3353 and claimant did not sustain any injuries in the alleged accident.
The owner of the vehicle has failed to intimate about the accident to respondent No.1.

The owner has failed to produce the insurer the relevant documents such as RC, FC, DL, etc., to establish the vehicle was road worthy and was ridden by a rider holding a valid and effective DL to drive that very specified class of vehicle.

The owner has consciously permitted a non licence to drive the vehicle in flagrant violation of the express terms of the policy and statute section 3 and section 5 of the MV Act This respondent submits that if the owner furnishes all relevant documents and it is noticed that the owner has not violated any of the terms and conditions of the policy, then this respondent would submit that their liability if any, is as per the terms and conditions of the policy.
It is further contended that all other averments of the claim petition not specifically traversed are denied as false.
Hence respondent No.1 prays to dismissal of the claim petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1.
Whether the petitioners prove that the deceased Jagadeesha T.R. sustained Kamalamma vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108172127/

sentences.text: 2 grievous injury in an accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.HR38Y3353 on 10122020 at about 10.00 p.m. to 10.05 p.m. near Seebi Forest Maruthi Daba, Tumakuru, Sira NH 48, Sira Taluk, Tumkur he succumbed to the said injury?
2. Whether the petitioners prove that they are legal representatives of the deceased ?
3. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?
If so, how much and from whom ?
4. What order or award ?
5. The Petitioner No.2 examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 24 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents have not lead either oral or documentary evidence.
6. Arguments were addressed on both sides.
7. Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is only with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioners plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the Lorry bearing reg.No.HR38Y3353.
Whereas the respondent No.1 contending that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.

9. It can be seen from the complaint of Hanumantharaju that at the time of the accident, the lorry bearing Reg.No.HR 38Y3353 has stationed the lorry on the track of the road without putting indicator and also without placing any barricade for giving any signal or to warn other road users and due to the rash and negligent way of stationing of the vehicle on road, the deceased who was riding the motor cycle on the left side of the lorry could not see the lorry in the dark night and hit to the lorry and thereby accident has been caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of the lorry.
The Kallambella police after due investigation filed charge sheet against driver of lorry for the offences punishable u/s's 283, 304A of IPC.

Apart from this, on perusal of the sketch and spot mahazar ExP4 it clearly shows that the accident had been taken place on the 3 rd track of the road and it also reveals that the lorry was stationed on the middle of the 3 rd track road.
If at all the lorry was not stationed on the road or else stationed on the mud road or end of the road, the accident would not have been taken place.

During cross examination, PW.1 was suggested that the accident Kamalamma vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108172127/
3 took place due to negligence of the deceased, which was outrightly denied.

sentences.text: 10. On the other hand, respondent No.1 has raised the contention that lorry was parked on the road as the Tyre of the lorry was burst.
But in this regard, the suggestion of respondent No.1 was denied by the PW1.

Apart from this, on perusal of IMV report marked at ExP6, it does not reveals that any tyre of the lorry was burst on that day and ExP6 reveals that on that day the accident has not caused due to the any mechanical defect of the above said vehicles.
Apart from this on perusal of mahazar ExP4, it reveals that at the time of the seziure of the lorry, the tyre of the lorry was not burst.
If at all the tyre of the lorry was burst, certainly the same would have been mentioned in the ExP4 also.

Moreover as per the FIR, ExP1 and also ExP3 charge sheet soon after the accident,
the driver of the lorry without giving any information to the police took away the lorry from spot.
The very conduct of the accused that is the driver of the lorry itself shows that the accident has been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry.

11. Further though respondent No.1 has taken the contention that on that day triangular reflector and hazard light was put on by the driver of the lorry for indicating that the lorry was stationed on the road.

But on perusal of ExP1 FIR and also ExP4spot mahazar it does not reveals that any triangular reflector or barricade or any indicator was stationed at the spot and also any hazarder light was put to indicate the parking of the lorry.
However the respondent counsel has not disputed the fact that the lorry was parked on the road.
Even respondent No.1 counsel has failed to examine the driver of the lorry who has to give the reasons or who has to explain the situations why he has parked the lorry on the road.

12. Apart from this, if at all as per the version of the respondent, tyre of the lorry was burst, how could the driver of the lorry, soon after the accident would have drove the lorry from the spot and absconded which is highly improbable.
Moreover the respondent No.1 did not make any attempt to examine the driver of offending lorry, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Nonexamination of driver of offending vehicle is fatal to the defence of Respondent No.1.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of lorry has to be disbelieved.

13. The evidence and material on record, clearly shows that lorry was stationed on the road without keeping any barricades, reflectors and signals to safeguard the interest on the traffic moving on the road and apart from this, it was dark night.

Precautions prescribed under Section 122 of MV Act read with the relevant Rules have to be followed by the driver and owner of the stationed vehicle,
particularly on a highway.

A duty is cast on the driver as well as the owner of such a vehicle to ensure that such a vehicle is towed away as immediately as practicable and not left abandoned or unattended, particularly on a highway where vehicles are permitted to move at a faster pace than on other roads.

In the alternative, some other form of external lighting ought to have been provided so as to give an indication about the parked lorry, until a vehicle, which is stationed/parked due to a break down or if it has met with an accident is towed away, it is necessary that the said vehicle does not become dangerous to other vehicles.

sentences.text: 15. In view of the ratio held in the above decision in the present case, admittedly lorry was stationed on the road without any sign or indication to warn other road users.
Moreover it was dark night.

Under such circumstances, certainly, it can be held that accident had been caused wholly due to the negligence on the driver of the lorry who had parked the lorry on the road without any indicator and barricade.

Moreover, ti is the burden on the driver of the lorry to state the circumstances and the explanations as to under what circumstances, he had parked the lorry on the road, but in the present case, respondent No.1 has not examined the driver of the lorry which is fatal to the case of respondent No.1.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the lorry bearing No.HR38 Y3353.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. ISSUES NO.2 & 3 :
The petitioner No.2 filed affidavit in lieu of his chiefexamination and deposed that he is the son, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.3 is the son of the deceased.
The documents which are exhibited at Ex's.P10 to 15 i.e., adhaar card, pan card and ration card reflect the aforesaid relationship of the claimants with the deceased.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents, as is evident from the tenor of cross examination of PW.1.

Be that as it may, since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
17. LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS:
In the Aadhaar card (Ex.P.10) the date of birth of deceased is shown as 951974, which indicates that he was aged 46 years on the date of accident.
Admittedly the deceased was married and as per the date of birth shown in the Ex P10Adhaar card, ExP13pan card and ExP17DL, at the time of accident he was 46 years of age.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '13'.
18.
According to PW.1, the deceased was working in Shahi Exports private limited as an Alteration operator and earning Rs.10,379/ and also agriculturist and earning Rs.10,000/ p.m.
The petitioner No.1 has produced ExP22 payslips and ExP23RTCs.
But the petitioners have not examined the person who issued the ExP22 to substantiate its contents.

From ExP20 mutation register and ExP23 RTC it reveals that land was not in the name of deceased Jagadeesha T.R.

sentences.text: Moreover no loss of income from the agriculture does not arise, as PW1 himself admitted in his crossexamination admitted that petitioner No.1 is doing agriculture and deriving the income from the agriculture.

19. The petitioners have stated that deceased was working at Shahi Exports private limited as an Alteration operator and earning Rs.10,379/ and produced the salary slips from June to December as per ExP22 .
But the petitioner has not examined the person who issued the said salary slips to substantiate its contents.
In the absence of proof, this Court has to consider the income notionally for calculating the compensation.

As the accident took place in the year 2020 and since the deceased was a semi skilled worker, the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.12,000/ p.m.
Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the deceased, nature of his work as well as the present cost of living.

20. In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

entities.text: 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per Sarala Verma's case towards his future prospectus if 25% of the salary is added it would be around Rs.15,000/ (12,000 + 3000).
The deceased was married and having three dependents.
Hence 1/3rd of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.

1/3 of Rs.15,000/
works out to Rs.5,000/.
Income for consideration is Rs.10,000/ (15,000 - 5,000).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,20,000/ (10,000 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '13'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.15,60,000/ (1,20,000 X 13).
21. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/ (in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.40,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017)

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: on account of loss of spousal consortium, parental consortium and loss of love & affection.
22. LOSS OF ESTATE:

Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case,
10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards loss of estate.
23. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,150/ ( in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.15,000/ has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) towards funeral expenses.

24. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : 15,60,00000 2 Loss of Consortium : 1,45,20000 3 Loss of Estate : 18,15000 4 Funeral Expenses : 18,15000 Total Rs.17,41,500=00 Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.17,41,500=00.
25.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

sentences.text: There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Though the insurance company contended that the owner of lorry bearing Reg.No.H.R.38Y3353 has violated the terms & conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms & conditions of the policy by the respondent No.1.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
27. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the findings given on issues No.1 to 3 and for the reasons discussed therein, I proceed to pass the following;
: ORDER : The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.17,41,500=00 with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 80  %
 Petitioner No.2 10  %
 Petitioner No.3 10  %
Out of the share amount of Petitioner No.1 a sum equal to 40% shall be deposited in her name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of her choice for a period of 5 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to her through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner No.2 and 3 through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw an award accordingly.
